newsitem.title: UK: Portillo echoes calls for UK Conservative unity.
newsitem.headline: Portillo echoes calls for UK Conservative unity.

text.p: Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, eschewing the strident nationalist rhetoric for which he was criticised at last year's Conservative conference, appealed on Thursday for the party to unite to defeat Labour at the coming election.
"One thing that has always marked the Conservative party apart is its will to govern and its determination to win.

"But I tell this conference, in order to win we need three extra policies -- unity, unity and unity," Portillo said, in an echo of Labour leader Tony Blair's pledge to make "education, education and education" his top three priorities.

Attacking Blair for his former membership of the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmamnt, Portillo asked rhetorically: "Should we not worry about the judgement of one who was so totally wrong? And worry more about his candour?
"Labour showed no judgement in the past. It shows no principles today."
In a speech that steered clear of the controversial issue of Europe, Portillo warned that a Labour government would cut Britain's defence spending.
"Dogs bark. Birds sing. Labour governments cut defence," he said.
